slot.brief: Multi-step: alkyl halide → elimination → addition of HBr (peroxide effect question) → substitution; identify the final product structure after the full sequence.

stem: 1-Bromobutane is heated with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$; the alkene formed is treated with $\text{HBr}$ in peroxide, then with $\text{NaI}$ in acetone. What is the final product?

verdicts.working: Alcoholic KOH eliminates HBr to form but-1-ene. Peroxide-assisted addition of HBr gives 1-bromobutane; NaI in acetone substitutes Br with I, forming 1-iodobutane.

working:
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}\xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{alc. KOH}}\text{CH}_2{=}\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$.\n$\text{HBr}/\text{peroxide}$ adds anti-Markovnikov: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$.\n$\text{NaI}/\text{acetone}$ substitutes Br by I, giving 1-iodobutane.

Independent check: Alcoholic KOH eliminates HBr to form but-1-ene. Peroxide-assisted addition of HBr gives 1-bromobutane; NaI in acetone substitutes Br with I, forming 1-iodobutane.
solution:
Alcoholic KOH causes elimination, and peroxide-assisted HBr addition is anti-Markovnikov:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH},\ \Delta} \text{CH}_2{=}\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{HBr}/\text{peroxide}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$$
NaI in acetone replaces Br with I, giving 1-iodobutane.
